topic: Pulsars — the cosmic lighthouses that almost weren't believed

beats.narration: In 1967, a graduate student found a signal that pulsed every 1.3 seconds.
beats.image_prompt: 1960s radio telescope array under a clear night sky, documentary style, dramatic lighting, no people

beats.narration: Jocelyn Bell Burnell and her advisor first joked it might be little green men — then ruled that out.
beats.image_prompt: vintage radio astronomy chart with regular pulse spikes on paper, scientific instrument aesthetic, no people

beats.narration: It was a pulsar: a rapidly spinning neutron star sweeping a beam of radio waves past Earth.
beats.image_prompt: artist concept of a neutron star pulsar emitting twin beams of radiation in deep space, cinematic, no people

beats.narration: The 1974 Nobel Prize went to her supervisor. Bell Burnell was left off the prize — a decision still widely criticized.
beats.image_prompt: deep space nebula with a bright pulsing stellar object, epic cosmic wide shot, no people
